source_title: Halle Berry’s Modified Custody Arrangement to ‘Temporarily’ Continue as Ex’s Restraining Order Denied amid Child Abuse Accusations: Source - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actress was accused by her ex-husband Olivier Martinez of abusing their 13-year-old son Maceo
Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic; Jenny Anderson/Getty
Halle Berry’s modified custody arrangement over her son Maceo, 13, will stay in place after a judge denied ex Olivier Martinez’s domestic violence restraining order request against the actress
The judge also dissolved Martinez’s temporary restraining order after nearly two weeks of custody hearings
Berry and Martinez will return to court in November for their 13-year-old son Maceo’s custody review
Halle Berry ’s modified custody arrangement over son Maceo will stay in place after her ex-husband Olivier Martinez’s restraining order was dissolved, a source tells PEOPLE.
Since Monday, Oct. 19, Berry and Martinez have been attending hearings over Martinez’s request for a restraining order against the actress to protect him and their 13-year-old son, Maceo.
Now, an insider tells PEOPLE that after nearly two weeks of testimony, Martinez’s temporary restraining order has been dissolved and his request for a domestic violence restraining order has been denied.
Berry and Martinez’s current custody arrangement, which modified the hours of visitation between Berry and Maceo, has been temporarily extended. The agreement will remain in place until November, when the two parties are called back to the courtroom to reexamine their custody arrangement.

“We are extremely pleased that the Court has dissolved the TRO,” Marina Beck, attorney for Berry, said in a statement. “As we move forward, Halle is determined to continue to focus on the well-being and best interest of her family.”
A rep for Martinez did not immediately respond to PEOPLE’s request for comment.
On Oct. 1, Berry was accused by Martinez of being violent toward their son Maceo. Martinez filed for sole custody of Maceo, claiming that Berry “physically abused” him in a Sept. 26 incident and alleging “other instances of abuse” in recent years.
That same day, a judge ordered temporarily modified visitation , writing that partial custody is to be “continued to maintain communication between [Berry] and [Maceo], while denying a request that Berry’s sobriety be monitored, citing “insufficient information.”
The order also modified the hours of Berry’s visitation with Maceo to limit her time with him to Mondays and Tuesdays between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m., and Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Earlier this month, Berry objected to her son Maceo testifying in court during the former couple’s upcoming custody hearings. She claimed that Martinez was dismissing statements from other key eyewitnesses, including her daughter Nahla Ariela , 18, and her fiancé Van Hunt , who were physically present at the time of the alleged Sept. 26 incident.
In other court documents obtained by PEOPLE, Martinez said that Maceo wants to address the court “to provide his side of the story.” He explained that Maceo wants to openly discuss his custody preferences and the alleged incident from September.
“He should have the opportunity to have his voice heard regarding what he experienced that night,” Martinez wrote in his declaration. “If he is prevented from addressing the Court regarding these allegations, I fear that he would be dissuaded from reporting problems or potential abuse in the future.”
A judge ruled that Berry and Martinez’s son Maceo could testify in his parents’ custody trial, but his testimony would be “limited to the request for an issuance of a restraining order.” Maceo testified in a closed hearing earlier this month.
Since the news broke, Berry has denied the abuse allegations , saying she is a victim of domestic violence herself. In a declaration filed on Monday, Oct. 5, and obtained by PEOPLE, Berry stated, “I have never physically, emotionally, or otherwise abused Maceo. I am a victim of domestic violence, and I help victims of domestic violence.”
She continued, “I am not a perpetrator of violence. I would never hurt our child.”
Martinez previously told PEOPLE in a statement, “My paramount concern is and always has been the health, welfare, and safety of our son, Maceo. My actions are solely motivated by protecting him. I hope that Halle takes responsibility for whatever happened that night and keeps our son’s welfare in mind.”
